youtube.title: ROB SCOTT
youtube.summary: Southland District Mayor Rob Scott joins Rodney Hide to discuss the Government’s proposed local government reforms and why he believes the accelerated amalgamation process risks undermining local democracy. Scott outlines Southland’s existing plan to become a unitary authority, argues the Government’s three-month deadline leaves little room for meaningful public consultation and reflects on the challenges councils face under increasing central government direction. Discover the Southland Mayor on Facebook or on the Southland District Council website

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Winston Peters discusses NZ First's election campaign, arguing the party is gaining momentum despite media criticism. He outlines plans to expand offshore energy exploration, revive New Zealand's energy security and reform immigration settings. Peters also criticises the India free trade agreement, questions the closure of Marsden Point, comments on roadside drug testing, media independence and accountability and reiterates New Zealand First's opposition to gene technology while saying the party is still considering its position on the HSNO Amendment Bill.

youtube.title: ERIKA HARVEY
youtube.summary: Erika Harvey returns to discuss fresh legal action over the Tauranga Marine Precinct sale, arguing key questions about ownership of the wharf, public funding and the structure of the deal remain unanswered. She tells Paul Brennan that court action is now needed to clarify who owns the wharf. For more information: Check out the Lobby for Good substack – Tauranga was told to move on. The money trail says we should look closer For more from Erika or Lobby For Good or find Lobby for Good on X For everything you need to know about the local body elections visit Council Watch

youtube.title: JASON WATSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with registered nurse Jason Watson about his peer-reviewed article on suicidality in transgender-identifying individuals, which was withdrawn from the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Journal shortly after publication. Jason discusses his analysis of the evidence behind gender-affirming care, the influence of the Cass Review, concerns about affirmation-only clinical approaches and the role of research in challenging accepted practice. CONTENT WARNING: This interview discusses the sensitive topic of suicide/self-harm. Listener discretion is advised.

youtube.title: TE KIRA LAWRENCE
youtube.summary: Napier City councillor Te Kira Lawrence joins Maree Buscke to discuss Hawke's Bay's proposal to pursue a single unitary authority under the Government's local government reforms. They explore why public sentiment appears to have shifted since previous amalgamation referendums, weighing potential efficiencies against concerns over representation, centralisation and the lack of detailed information available. Lawrence also explains her decision to stand as a New Zealand First candidate in the upcoming general election. You can find more on Te Kira: On the Napier City Council website and Te Kira Lawrence NCC Facebook page Or on the New Zealand First website and Te Kira Lawrence NZ First Facebook page

youtube.title: THE FOURTH ESTATE
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined on The Fourth Estate by David Harvey and Peter Williams for a wide-ranging media wrap: TVNZ's baffling choice to bury Ryan Fox's British Open win behind FIFA World Cup coverage, redundancies rippling through Stuff and the Herald, suppression orders around the Pauline Hanna inquest and the Māori roll debate. They also take aim at “fear porn” journalism around bird flu and weather warnings, before touching on Paul Henry and Michael Laws's political comebacks ahead of November's election. Sign up for RCR Bites News

youtube.title: CAMERON MURRAY
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with Dr Cameron Murray, Chief Economist at Fresh Economic Thinking, about the assumptions driving Australia's housing debate. Dr Murray challenges popular narratives around affordability, supply shortages, immigration and first-home ownership, arguing that interest rates, credit creation and inflation have far greater influence on housing prices than commonly believed. For further information: Visit Fresh Economic Thinking or find them on YouTube Find Dr Cameron Murray on X Discover more from Michael Arbon on Facebook and X

youtube.title: UNDER THE HOOD
youtube.summary: Graham Hood explores how parents shape their children's future relationships by the example they set at home. Reflecting on his own experiences, Hoody argues that a strong marriage provides children with security, stability and a healthy model for adult life. He challenges modern child-centred parenting, emphasising that prioritising the marital relationship ultimately benefits the whole family. Discover more from Hoody at Club Grubbery or find him on Facebook and X

youtube.title: THE BRENNAN BAROMETER
youtube.summary: From politicians to reporters, Paul Brennan takes a satirical look at New Zealand's hi-vis obsession, asking whether safety culture has become more about performance than protection. Sign up for RCR Bites News

youtube.title: MICHAEL ARBON
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon examines Australia's housing shortfall, arguing the Albanese government's target of building 1.2 million homes in five years is slipping further out of reach. Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: LIFE IS MENTAL
youtube.summary: Meagan McNamara and Jen Bainbridge explore extreme beauty trends, including salmon sperm facial treatments, and discuss celebrity culture, media priorities, elite circles and the Epstein files. They also examine a controversial Ellen DeGeneres segment and the broader questions it raises about the stories that dominate headlines. Sign up for RCR Bites News

youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Natalie Cutler-Welsh is joined by natural health practitioner Karen Creighton for a wide-ranging webinar challenging popular health wisdom. From peptides and cholesterol to statins, exercise and thyroid function, Karen unpacked why standard blood test numbers often mislead, pointing instead to triglyceride-to-HDL ratios and liver health as the real story behind fatigue, weight gain and hormonal chaos. The conversation closed with a striking, more speculative claim about EMFs and biofields, alongside her own wellness remedy, Living Resilience. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They are not intended as medical or health advice, and do not constitute personalised diagnosis, treatment, or recommendations. Listeners should seek guidance from their trusted healthcare provider for advice tailored to their individual circumstances. Karen is offering RCR listeners a special price for her Living Blueprint Duo – helping your body remember what it was designed to do. Just $99! Check out Karen’s slide show Health-Myths

youtube.title: JENNY HORST
youtube.summary: Simon O'Connor speaks with Jenny Horst, CEO of Upside Youth Mentoring, about helping young people thrive through meaningful relationships rather than more screen time. They discuss the growing impact of social media on youth wellbeing, the importance of real-world connection and practical ways parents can strengthen family relationships through shared experiences, play and everyday conversations. For more information: Visit the Upside Website Check out Community youth mentoring or Online youth mentoring Find Upside on Facebook and Jenny Horst on LinkedIn

youtube.title: HARVEY WEAKE
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Harvey Weake, a 30-year petrochemical industry veteran, about Winston Peters’ proposal to expand offshore energy mapping. Harvey supports the policy but argues New Zealand must first rebuild its energy institutions through a dedicated Ministry of Energy with the expertise to develop a coherent national strategy. Stay up to date. Sign up for RCR Bites News

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart argues that the media and public institutions wrongly portray the so-called “rainbow community” as a single, unified group, ignoring the diversity of views among gay people. She criticises Pride events, activist politics, and local government support for Pride initiatives, contending they have become divisive, overly sexualised, and increasingly out of step with many New Zealanders. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X
